findings.explanation: In the UCSM object model vnicEtherIf is the per-VLAN interface (rn `if-[name]`) and has no failoverEnabled property. Fabric failover is configured on vnicEther itself through switchId values `A-B` or `B-A` (allowed values: A, A-B, B, B-A, NONE). detailedImplementation Step 3 (3) and Step 5 item 3 repeat the wrong mapping.
findings.suggested_fix: State that fabric placement and failover both come from vnicEther.switchId (A, B, A-B, B-A), and drop vnicEtherIf from the failover logic.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS assigns all data sourcetype `cisco:ucs` and puts the class in source (`cisco:ucs:vnicEther`, `cisco:ucs:lsServer`); detailedImplementation's 'keep sourcetype cisco:ucs:inventory' and 'expect cisco:ucs:inventory' are therefore wrong for a default install.
findings.suggested_fix: Document `sourcetype=cisco:ucs source=cisco:ucs:vnicEther OR source=cisco:ucs:lsServer`, or say explicitly that `cisco:ucs:inventory` is a local override set on the input.

findings.explanation: The add-on documentation uses `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs/local/` and the Splunkbase app id is `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs` (hyphen); the inputs.conf path given in detailedImplementation would target a non-existent app directory.
findings.quote: The on-disk directory name and canonical app id use an underscore.

findings.explanation: Class IDs are selected in add-on collection Templates (Configuration > Templates or `splunk_ta_cisco_ucs_templates.conf` `content=`), which inputs reference with `templates=`; there is no inventory stanza with a `url=` key or a class-list setting in inputs.conf.
findings.quote: In the add-on’s advanced or class-list surface for the XML inventory poller, ensure vnicEther, vnicEtherIf, and lsServer are not removed
findings.suggested_fix: Describe adding a Manager, a Template containing vnicEther and lsServer, and an Input that references both.

findings.explanation: The SPL raises critical when operable vNICs exist on only one fabric and warning when both fabrics are used with no failover; 'count >= 1' is not the alert condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the critical/warning states in plain words.

findings.explanation: The Network Management Guide reference points at the Cisco home page.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco UCS Manager Network Management Guide 4.2 — vNIC, Ethernet interfaces",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual UCSM 4.2 Network Management Guide vNIC chapter.

findings.explanation: Template text with a stray `]` field and no real causes; the genuine false positives (approved single-NIC appliances, lab orgs, template clones mid-edit, poll during FI failover) are already listed in exclusions and Step 5 but not here.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `sp_dn`, `parent`, `]` — Health checks in `cisco_ucs` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the concrete causes from Step 5 and exclusions into knownFalsePositives.

findings.explanation: Marked verified although the SPL depends on attributes that do not exist on the MOs it reads, so it cannot produce a non-info row.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until tested against real vnicEther inventory.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: is_op reads operState from vnicEther rows, but vnicEther has no operState property (operState is on vnicEtherIf). is_op is always 0, so vnic_count_a/vnic_count_b are always 0 and every profile lands in unknown_topology/info; critical and warning can never fire.

failover_enabled_count is built from vnicEtherIf.failoverEnabled, a property that does not exist; fabric failover is vnicEther.switchId in (A-B, B-A). The sw="a"/"b" tests also ignore A-B/B-A values, so failover-enabled vNICs are never counted on either fabric.
Base and subsearches use sourcetype="cisco:ucs:inventory"; the add-on's default sourcetype is cisco:ucs (class in source), so the search returns nothing without a local override.

The sp_dn regex `^(?<sp_dn>org-root/.+?/ls-[^/]+)` and the org replace require a sub-org, so service profiles directly under org-root (org-root/ls-NAME) are never joined to their vNICs; the nested join/subsearch pattern is also subject to subsearch result limits on large domains.

summary: The southbound A/B vNIC posture idea and the sibling boundaries are clearly written, but the UCSM object facts are wrong: vnicEtherIf has no failoverEnabled attribute (fabric failover is encoded as vnicEther switchId A-B/B-A) and vnicEther has no operState, so the SPL counts zero operable vNICs and classifies every profile as unknown_topology. The add-on facts (sourcetype, app folder, class-list configuration) also contradict the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS documentation.
